output.summary: The claim was denied as not medically necessary under the ER coverage clause. To pursue the viable appeal, gather additional medical evidence and follow the outlined steps.

items.text: Obtain a physician letter of medical necessity to support that the ER visit was required.
Provide clinical progress notes from the treating physician documenting symptom severity.
Request a peer‑to‑peer review with the insurer’s medical director.
Gather the physician letter and attach it to the appeal.
Include the clinical progress notes with the appeal packet.
Schedule and document a peer‑to‑peer review as part of the appeal process.
The DME precedent (F-DME-NECESSITY) does not apply because it concerns durable medical equipment, not emergency room services, and is governed by C-2025-DME-NECESSITY.
The physiotherapy precedent (F-PHYSIO-NECESSITY) is irrelevant; it addresses physiotherapy limits under C-2025-PHYSIO-LIMIT, not ER coverage.
The physiotherapy notes precedent (F-PHYSIO-NOTES) also pertains to physiotherapy limits (C-2025-PHYSIO-LIMIT) and cannot be used for this ER claim.
No gates are listed, but ensure the appeal is submitted within the policy’s appeal window to avoid procedural denial.
